title: On Reduction Probability Models in Lattice Sieving
abstract:
In lattice sieving, the sphere model assumes that sieving elements are distributed close to or on a sphere with uniformly distributed direction.
It is extensively used to predict how lattice sieving behaves.
In the sphere model the probability that a random pair of vectors reduces is asymptotically $p_n={(3/4)}^{n/2}/\sqrt{3\pi n/8}$.
In practice sieving algorithms have been observed to perform better than predicted by the sphere model.
It is an open question how this gap behaves asymptotically: does the gap vanish or grow as the dimension grows?

Our work answers this question by showing that it is asymptotically constant.
We generalise the sphere model to uniform ball and non-uniform ball models and analyse reduction probability distributions.
We find that asymptotically the input distribution only affects the total reduction probability, not the shape of the output length distribution.
We show that the reduction probability advantages of our models over the sphere model range from $\times 1.5$ up to $\times 8$.

1   Introduction
Consider a lattice L and let λ1 be the length of its shortest non-zero vector.
Finding a vector v ∈ L \ {0} such that ∥v∥ = λ1 is known as the Shortest
Vector Problem (SVP). Lattice sieving methods aim to solve SVP (or to find a
sufficiently short vector) by maintaining a large list L of lattice elements, and
repeatedly trying to find reducing pairs: i.e., x, y ∈ L with distance D(x, y) =
∥x−y∥ ‘small’, and then adding x−y to the list (replacing either x, y, whichever
is longer, or the longest element from the list).
    In this work, we study models to analyse the probability that a pair re-
duces, as well as the distribution of the norms of the reductions found. Nguyen-
Vidick [NV08] introduced the heuristic assumption that the list follows an isotropic
distribution close to (or on) a sphere of radius r, that we refer to as the sphere
model, and obtain an asymptotic expression for the reduction probability:

                  Pr[∥x − y∥ ≤ r] ∼ pn := 43           / 3πn/8.

Without loss of generality, we will use r = 1, i.e., the unit sphere as we can
always rescale a lattice. An exact expression for the reduction probability uses
the regularized incomplete beta function (e.g. [FBB+ 15]):

The sphere model is used extensively throughout the lattice sieving literature,
because of its simplicity and due to the fact that the mass of an n-dimensional
ball concentrates at its boundary as n → ∞. Indeed, this can be observed from
the uniform distribution on the n-dimensional ball, which has length PDF f (x) =
nxn−1 , that vanishes pointwise for any length x < 1 as n → ∞.
    However, in practice lattice sieving has been observed to perform better than
expected given the sphere model, and it is an open question how this gap be-
haves asymptotically [AGPS20, ABD+ 21]. Does this gap vanish, or grow as the
dimension grows? Our work answers this open question by presenting ball mod-
els and showing that the gap is asymptotically constant, with different constants
for various cases.
    Asymptotically, it seems that all radial information is lost from n-dimensional
balls, and only the directional distribution is needed. However, analysing the
scaled depth w := (1 − x)n, instead of lengths x, one finds that asymptotically
the distribution of the scaled depth tends to the exponential distribution Exp(1):

This motivates us to look for better models that take the length distribution
into account and to compare their advantage with the sphere model.
    In this work we generalise the sphere model to the ball model and study
both the uniform ball distribution and non-uniform ball distributions. For the
uniform ball distribution, we derive equally simple asymptotic expressions for
the reduction probability as for the sphere model. Non-uniform ball distributions
enable the analysis of iterated sieving rounds: the output distribution of one
round is the input distribution of the next, and we obtain results in terms of
scaled depths. We find two cases where the output scaled depth distribution
always tends to the exponential distribution Exp(2/3), for which we also derive
asymptotic reduction probability expressions.


1.1   Contributions

We introduce a framework and tools to analyse the ball model for four slightly
different sieving processes. We distinguish on two distance functions:

 – Fixed sign: only ∥x − y∥ is considered (or alternatively ∥x + y∥):

                        D- (x, y) := ∥x − y∥    ≤ ∥x∥ + ∥y∥

 – Optimised sign: ∥x − y∥ and ∥x + y∥ are considered, using the shortest:

But we also distinguish on the reduction criteria:

 – Local reductions: (x, y) is a reducing pair ⇔ D(x, y) ≤ max(∥x∥, ∥y∥), when

2    Lattice Sieving
We study reduction models of lattice sieving under the Gaussian heuristic. The
Gaussian heuristic implies that the distribution of lattice elements is isotropic
(i.e. the distribution has no directional bias), since it estimates the number of
contained lattice elements purely based on volume.
